name: North Dakota
tagline: From the Badlands and Missouri breaks to the Turtle Mountains and Pembina Gorge.
intro: North Dakota's byways drop below the prairie into the valleys of the Sheyenne, the James and the Pembina, follow the Missouri past old trading posts and village sites, and wind through the western Badlands. This chapter follows the state's Scenic Byways and Backways as listed by North Dakota Tourism, a program whose first three roads were designated in 1997. The state calls its shorter, partly gravel routes backways, and lists the North Dakota end of the two-state Native American Scenic Byway under the name Standing Rock National Native American Scenic Byway.

programs.label: North Dakota Scenic Byways and Backways

members.name: Chan SanSan Scenic Backway
members.blurb: South of Highway 46 the backway drops into the James River valley and follows it down through LaMoure County, past Grand Rapids and LaMoure, a double pony truss bridge and old earthen mounds in the tall grass.

members.name: Des Lacs National Wildlife Refuge Scenic Backway
members.blurb: Thirteen miles north through the Des Lacs refuge from US 52 near Kenmare, along lakes where more than 250 bird species have been counted, bald eagles come through in fall and moose turn up in the brush.

members.name: Killdeer Mountain Four Bears Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Sixty-four miles from north of Manning up Highway 22 through Killdeer, past the Killdeer Mountains and their battlefield site, then east on Highway 23 over the Little Missouri breaks to New Town and the Four Bears Museum.

members.name: Sakakawea Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 200A keeps to the high ground above the Missouri between Washburn and Stanton on the line of Lewis and Clark's journey, past Fort Clark and the Knife River Indian Villages.

members.name: Old Red Old Ten Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The old Red Trail, later Highway 10, runs beside I-94 from Mandan to Dickinson through small farm towns, past Salem Sue at New Salem and Assumption Abbey at Richardton, with a gravel stretch before Glen Ullin.

members.name: Rendezvous Region Scenic Backway
members.blurb: Out of Walhalla, a few miles below the Manitoba line, the backway follows the bends of the Pembina River into the Pembina Gorge, a deep valley holding one of the largest unbroken woodlands in North Dakota.

members.name: Sheyenne River Valley National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Sixty-three miles down the Sheyenne valley from Baldhill Dam through Valley City and Fort Ransom to Lisbon, in a glacial meltwater trench up to 330 feet deep that comes as a surprise after the flat fields above.

members.name: Standing Rock National Native American Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the Cannonball River south on Highways 1806 and 24 to the South Dakota line, the road crosses the Standing Rock Sioux Reservation above the Missouri, through Fort Yates in the country where Sitting Bull lived and died.

members.name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park North Unit Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Fourteen miles in from US 85 south of Watford City, the park road runs along the floor of the badlands, climbs to River Bend Overlook and its CCC shelter, then follows the rim out to Oxbow Overlook.

members.name: Turtle Mountain Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From north of Rolla, Highway 43 runs west through the wooded lake country of the Turtle Mountains, by Lake Upsilon and Lake Metigoshe, then comes down onto open prairie at Highway 14.
